newsitem.title: GERMANY: Stephan Hermlin, top writer in ex-E.Germany, dies.
newsitem.headline: Stephan Hermlin, top writer in ex-E.Germany, dies.

text.p: Stephan Hermlin, one of former communist East Germany's leading writers, has died aged 81, his publishers said on Monday.

The essayist and lyricist, whose most famous works include the prose collection "Evening Light" and short story collection "Decisions", died in Berlin on Sunday, the Wagenbach-Verlag publishing house said.

Hermlin came from a wealthy family but joined the Communist Party in 1931. He said it was his life's task to defend art from its dogmatic despisers but he did not distance himself from communism even after the unification of Germany in 1990.

"I recognise that I belong to a generation whose hopes have collapsed but that does not mean that these hopes have stopped," Hermlin said in one of his last interviews after the fall of the Berlin Wall.

Hermlin emigrated from Germany in 1936 and fought in the Spanish Civil War and then the French resistance movement against the Nazis. He returned to Germany in 1945 and lived in East Berlin from 1947.
